SidC A3 performs intermodular L-AHO loading and A2 can catalyze noncanonical Gly ligation.
SidC C3 acts as a chain-length gatekeeper favoring tripeptide intermediates.
C. graminicola cluster 38 is identical in gene content/order to a RADS cluster and native C. graminicola produces radicicol/monocillins.
Direct knockout evidence for radicicol biosynthetic genes cited in the record comes from another fungus, not C. graminicola.
Native C. graminicola BGC-to-product causality therefore remains untested by pathway-specific genetics.
The atn cluster is causally linked to arthripenoid biosynthesis by gene inactivation and heterologous/biochemical experiments.
AtnH/AtnG form the polyketide core, followed by AtnJ oxidative decarboxylation and AtnF farnesylation.
AtnK and AtnA sequentially epoxidize the farnesyl chain and AtnI catalyzes tricyclic ring formation.
Arthripenoid C is partly downstream of a chemically labile arthripenoid-B-derived intermediate; not every terminal congener requires a dedicated enzyme.
The retired/SQ_A MIBiG status does not negate the strong experimental pathway evidence.
Full-length fum clusters occur in fumonisin-producing A. welwitschiae isolates.
Some nonproducing A. welwitschiae isolates carry partial deletions of the fum cluster.
Cluster integrity alone is not universally sufficient to predict fumonisin production across black aspergilli.
The study does not perform A. welwitschiae pathway-specific knockout or heterologous reconstruction.
The anc cluster was identified and antrocin biosynthesis was characterized by heterologous expression.
AncC is a dual-functional HAD-like terpene cyclase that converts FPP to (+)-albicanol via an albicanyl-pyrophosphate intermediate.
AncA instead converts FPP to (R)-trans-gamma-monocyclofarnesol.
AncA Y283/F375 act as gatekeepers controlling cyclofarnesoid versus drimane-type scaffold formation.
Retired MIBiG status is database provenance and does not reduce confidence in the direct enzyme/pathway evidence.
Heterologous expression of fnsA in A. nidulans and S. cerevisiae establishes FnsA as a fungal naringenin synthetase.
Isotope feeding shows FnsA can use p-coumaric acid or p-hydroxybenzoic acid as starter units.
In-vitro assays show the FnsA adenylation domain activates both aromatic-acid starter units.
FnsA condenses p-coumaric acid with three malonyl-CoA units to naringenin; p-hydroxybenzoic acid uses four extensions to naringenin chalcone.
Engineered isorhamnetin/acacetin production is downstream synthetic-biology context and not a native P. fici BGC endpoint.
AstE, AstA and AstG sequentially form 5-methylorsellinic acid, DHMP and 5'-farnesyl-DHMP in A. oryzae.
AstF epoxidizes the farnesyl chain and AstH cyclizes the meroterpenoid scaffold.
AstI hydroxylates 13-deacetoxyaustalide I to 13-O-deacetylaustalide I.
AstB hydroxylation generates the hemiacetal-forming precursor and AstL SAM-dependent methylation constructs the orthoester of austalide B.
AstK hydroxylates austalide B to austalide F.
The proposed AstC Baeyer-Villiger oxidation was not successfully demonstrated in the heterologous system.
Database austalide T/U nomenclature is normalized separately from the underlying enzymatic evidence.
Expression of sesE, sesM and sesB in IDT-deficient P. paxilli produces prelecanindole.
sesE, sesM and sesB encode the core indole-prenyltransferase, FAD monooxygenase and terpene-cyclase functions required for IST formation.
SES-cluster enzymes can modify indole-diterpene substrates produced by the discrete TER cluster.
The canonical product set therefore includes molecules whose biosynthesis is not self-contained within the SES locus alone.
Current canonical organism naming differs from the defining paper's Tolypocladium album nomenclature.
Retired MIBiG status is kept separate from the strong heterologous pathway evidence.
Comparative long-read genomics identifies a PKS16-centered locus as the most likely gyrophoric-acid cluster across nine producing Umbilicaria species.
Only three genes are conserved across the candidate GA clusters, including the PKS gene.
The same candidate cluster family may underlie gyrophoric, umbilicaric and hiascic acid diversity.
No PKS16 knockout, heterologous reconstruction or purified-enzyme assay establishes direct gyrophoric-acid synthesis.
The study itself describes the locus as a candidate/most-likely cluster rather than experimentally validated causality.
MIBiG high/complete/retired status must therefore be separated from experimental validation depth.
Deletion of PDE_01235/OpdA eliminates oxopyrrolidines A and B, establishing the opd cluster as causal.
OpdC is required for product formation and is assigned as a trans-acting enoyl reductase for OpdA.
OpdJ is the cluster-specific transcription factor required for oxopyrrolidine production.
PscyB is a five-module NRPS required for cycloaspeptide A/E biosynthesis.
PscyA is a trans-acting N-methyltransferase that supplies methylated free amino-acid substrates to PscyB.
Coexpression of PscyA and PscyB in A. oryzae is sufficient to produce cycloaspeptides A and E.
VdoD catalyzes meta hydroxylation of cyclopenin to cyclopenol.
Cyclopenol rearranges to viridicatol spontaneously or through VdoA catalysis.
Direct conversion of viridicatin to viridicatol by VdoD was not detected.
N. discophora SNB-CN63 produces chlorinated ilicicolins and, under bromide OSMAC conditions, brominated analogues.
Whole-genome analysis nominates an ilicicolin-related BGC containing FAD-dependent halogenase Ndi_Ili_D.
No pathway-specific knockout or heterologous reconstruction establishes causal assignment of this locus.
A silent P. roqueforti BGC was causally assigned to annullatin biosynthesis through heterologous expression, gene deletion and feeding experiments.
The annullatin polyketide core undergoes sequential hydroxylation and prenylation.
A BBE-like enzyme catalyzes the terminal oxidative lactonization forming (2S,9S)-annullatin D.
Knockout of CgPKS4/Rsf1 abolishes detectable rasfonin production.
An NMR-verified rasfonin standard and spiking confirmed the wild-type chromatographic product identity.
Functions of most additional rsf-cluster genes are proposed from predicted enzyme classes rather than direct biochemical tests.
The eup2 locus is strongly linked to eupenifeldin-family biosynthesis by native production/expression and heterologous synthetic-biology reconstruction.
EupPKS/EupL1/EupL5 supply the tropolone branch while EupR3 supplies humulene and EupR1 mediates hetero-Diels–Alder chemistry.
Combinatorial substitution among eupenifeldin, pycnidione and xenovulene genes generates unnatural tropolone sesquiterpenoids.
DepD and DepH are both indispensable for formation of the depside precursor unguidepside A.
DepG catalyzes ether-bond formation converting bicyclic depsides to tricyclic depsidones, and DepF decarboxylates depsidone substrates.
Remotely encoded FAD halogenase A3428 catalyzes multiple halogenations culminating in nornidulin.
Heterologous expression of the M. phaseolina locus yields Macrollins A-D.
MacC catalyzes beta-carbon hydroxylation of tetramic-acid molecules.
SNB-CN111 produces chlorinated azaphilones and generates brominated and iodinated analogues under halide OSMAC conditions.
Genome mining nominates an azaphilone BGC containing FAD-dependent halogenase Psc_Aza_H.
No pathway-specific knockout or heterologous reconstruction establishes BGC-to-sclerotiorin causality in this strain.
crmA is required for production of fumicicolins and related N-formylvaline/valine-isocyanide metabolites in A. fumigatus.
Copper starvation induces the Crm programme and associated metabolite production.
The other three genes in the Af293 Crm cluster are not required for CrmA-dependent metabolites.
Crustosic acid formation through carboxylcrustic and viridicatic acid was confirmed by gene deletion and heterologous expression.
TraH converts crustosic acid toward terrestric acid by decarboxylation-mediated olefination.
TraD performs the subsequent reduction required for terrestric-acid formation and stereochemical outcome.
Heterologous expression of the cryptic locus yields soppilines A-C.
The pathway combines an HR-PKS with a type III PKS to generate alkylresorcinols with an unusual Z,E,Z-triene side chain.
Native activation conditions for the cryptic pathway were not established by the defining heterologous study.
GdlS heterologous expression and biochemical characterization produce germacradienol as the sole detected cyclase product.
GdlS strictly uses FPP and requires Mg2+ for catalytic activity.
Germacradienol and geosmin were not detected in native A. ustus 3.3904 under tested conditions.
Feeding germacradienol to native A. ustus did not establish conversion to geosmin or another detected product.
SatA cyclizes FPP to sativene.
SatB catalyzes C14-C15 oxidation followed by oxidative bond cleavage to seco-sativene intermediates.
SatC regioselectively reduces the C14 aldehyde and enables hemiacetal ring closure to prehelminthosporol.
The MIBiG physical record is partial even though the three-enzyme functional cassette is strongly resolved.
Deleting HDA1 causes approximately 1000-fold increased beauvericin and strong BEA1-3 upregulation.
BEA3 functions as an ABC-transporter-linked negative feedback component; its deletion elevates BEA1/BEA2 expression and beauvericin yield.
Bea4 and Yy1 act as repressors of the beauvericin programme.
Kmt6/H3K27 and Hda1-dependent chromatin state regulates accessibility of the BEA cluster, with increased H3K27ac in derepressed conditions.
The database's unknown physical completeness does not weaken the native causal evidence for BEA regulation and beauvericin output.
MpbA expression correlates with malpibaldin A-C production under LB plus fructose conditions.
Recombinant MpbA adenylation domains support the predicted module-specific amino-acid substrate preferences.
Antibiotic curing and 16S-based analyses argue against a bacterial endosymbiont as the source of the cyclopeptides.
No native MpbA whole-gene knockout was reported, so pathway attribution should not be promoted to knockout-grade necessity.
Heterologous TndC produces talarodiene, establishing the core diterpene-skeleton-forming enzyme.
13C-labeling defines a GGPP-to-talarodiene cyclization route through the bifunctional TndC enzyme.
Stable-isotope biotransformation supports talarodiene as a biosynthetic precursor of talaronoid C.
The downstream tailoring route from talarodiene to talaronoid C is not fully enzyme-resolved.
MpcA expression correlates with malpicyclin A-F production under LB plus fructose conditions.
Recombinant MpcA adenylation domains support predicted module-specific amino-acid substrate preferences.
Malpicyclins A-D were structurally characterized more completely than E-F, which remain primarily HRMS/MS-supported congeners.
Malpicyclins A-D show moderate antibacterial activity against tested Gram-positive bacteria, with MICs spanning 97.3-357.8 uM.
No native MpcA whole-gene knockout was reported, so pathway attribution remains high rather than knockout-grade.
NRPS4 overexpression induces fusahexin production in F. graminearum PH-1.
Fusahexin is a cyclic hexapeptide with an unusual ether bond linking Pro Cdelta to the preceding Thr Cbeta, forming an oxazine ring.
The five-module architecture of NRPS4 is proposed to generate the six-residue product by iterative use of the terminal module for two leucines.
The adjacent ABC transporter is cluster-associated, but its specific role in fusahexin biosynthesis/export was not directly established in the defining product study.
MIBiG marks the physical record partial, while the NRPS4-to-fusahexin causal assignment is strong.
Heterologous expression of the four-gene A. ruber cluster in A. nidulans yields echinulin and neoechinulin A as major products.
EchPT1 catalyzes the first reverse C2 prenylation of cyclo-L-Trp-L-Ala to preechinulin.
EchPT2 catalyzes consecutive further prenylations and is a major generator of echinulin-family structural diversity.
evidence_type_raw: purified enzyme assays + native extract confirmation

claim_text: EchP450 introduces only the C10-C11 double bond and therefore does not explain the second double bond of neoechinulin B-series products.
Preechinulin is a branching substrate: EchPT2 favors the saturated substrate, while EchP450 can divert it toward neoechinulin A followed by lower-regioselectivity prenylation.
The canonical record's QEN-0407-G2 label and taxon/reference-genome mapping to CBS 135680 represent a provenance mismatch that should not be collapsed into strain-specific direct genomic evidence.
Heterologous expression of the A. ustus ucd BGC produces new p-terphenyl derivatives and links the locus causally to the uscandidusin pathway.
Gene-deletion experiments support atromentin formation, reductive dehydration, O-methylation and prenylation as sequential pathway events.
Dibenzofuran formation yielding uscandidusin products occurs spontaneously from usterphenyllin-type precursors.
Recombinant UcdE directly prenylates dihydroxyterphenyllin and strongly favors substrates bearing an ortho-dihydroxyphenyl motif.
UcdB is proposed to catalyze reductive dehydration of atromentin; this assignment is supported genetically/pathway-wise but is less directly biochemically resolved than UcdE.
The canonical MIBiG class label should be retained as provenance while the mechanistic pathway is described as an NRPS-like atromentin/p-terphenyl programme.
Heterologous expression of the four-gene pbo cluster in A. nidulans establishes responsibility for (-)-protubonine B formation.
Gene deletions and isolated intermediates confirm the major biosynthetic sequence.
The recombinant flavin-dependent oxygenase performs stereospecific indole hydroxylation accompanied by pyrrolidine-ring formation.
The experimentally sufficient four-gene locus is narrower than the broader region retained by database provenance.
Standalone catalytic evidence is strongest for the flavin oxygenase; NRPS and acetyltransferase roles should not be represented as equivalently purified-enzyme proven.
The pba locus is causally linked to penindolene biosynthesis by heterologous expression, in vitro enzymology and CRISPR/Cas9 gene inactivation.
PbaC decarboxylates L-tryptophan to tryptamine.
PbaE prenylates tryptamine, and PbaD catalyzes an unusual secondary amide-forming condensation with L-glutamate.
PbaB catalyzes oxidative C2-C3 cleavage of the indole ring to produce two keto groups.
L-glutamic-acid feeding facilitated native product isolation but does not establish a natural ecological activation cue.
Antimicrobial and acetylcholinesterase-inhibitory activities were measured for the resolved penindolene stereoisomers.
Heterologous expression of the pho gene set reconstructs the phomoxanthone A pathway.
PhoCDEFGHK generate chrysophanol, which is processed by PhoBJKLMNP to penexanthone B.
A feeding experiment suggests PhoO catalyzes regioselective oxidative para-para coupling of penexanthone B to phomoxanthone A.
Native deletion of phoE eliminates phomoxanthone A production, independently confirming an essential role for the PKS in the native producer.
Current MIBiG retirement for validation failure invalidates use of the submitted physical record as current canonical locus evidence, but does not erase the experimentally supported Pho pathway.
Under standard laboratory conditions this strain predominantly produces phomoxanthone A, and deleting phoE shunts metabolism toward otherwise low-abundance monoterpene pathways.
Heterologous expression of the TTI001159 HX1035 cluster produces roseopurpurin C and establishes cluster-product causality.
prosJ alone produces 3-methylorsellinic acid and a depside intermediate, directly establishing the NR-PKS entry step.
Targeted core-gene disruption and transcription-factor overexpression in the homologous A. uvarum cluster identify the same roseopurpurin programme and reveal strong condition dependence.
Roseopurpurin C is an ATP-competitive CDK2 inhibitor with Kiapp 44 ± 8 nM.
The cluster-encoded CDK homolog prosG motivated resistance-gene-guided discovery, but its native self-resistance function is not equivalent to direct functional validation.
TF-overexpression and medium-response observations from A. uvarum must not be transferred as direct native regulation evidence for Phaeosphaeria TTI001159.
Reverse genetics and metabolomics link FmPKS8 to the fusamarin dihydroisocoumarin family.
FMAN_15220-FMAN_15223 form the functional four-gene cluster; deleting adjacent FMAN_15219 or FMAN_15224 does not affect compounds 1-9.
Synthetic ICI with 6 mM NaNO3 is productive, whereas glutamine and 120 mM nitrate conditions repress PKS8 in F. mangiferae.
FmKmt1/H3K9 methylation state influences FmPKS8 expression, providing direct chromatin-context evidence.
Regulation of PKS8 orthologs differs among Fusarium species; F. fujikuroi glutamine responses must not be transferred to MRC7560.
The broad MIBiG region is valid provenance, but functional cluster membership is experimentally narrowed to four genes.
Leptobacillium sp. CF-236968 naturally produces pycnidione, confirmed by HRMS and full NMR characterization.
Recombining tropolone-sesquiterpenoid pathway genes in A. oryzae reconstructs pycnidione-related scaffolds and demonstrates modular control over hetero-Diels-Alder coupling.
pycPKS, pycR6 and pycR1 respectively define the polyketide, humulene and hetero-Diels-Alder core modules of the locus.
Native activation conditions are not established by the synthetic-biology reconstruction.
The Stachybotrys sp. g12 orphan cluster produces alkyl salicylaldehyde derivatives including stachysalicyloid C.
StrA's KR domain catalyzes reductive chain release despite the absence of a C-terminal reductase domain.
StrC is critical for the aromatization reaction that forms the salicylaldehyde scaffold.
J. multiformis produces multiformin azaphilones, including A-J, in stromata.
Comparative genomics identifies a group-B azaphilone jmaza locus containing paired nrPKS/hrPKS and conserved tailoring genes.
The exact BGC0003113 physical record cannot be treated as current validated locus evidence because MIBiG marks it retired.
Heterologous expression of oesA produces 3-orsellinoxypropanoic acid.
OesA catalyzes both orsellinic-acid formation and transfer of the orsellinyl group to 3-hydroxypropanoic acid.
Both ACP domains contribute independently and complementarily to product formation.
Feeding data indicate that only the orsellinyl residue is acetate-derived.
Heterologous expression of the mfn gene set in Aspergillus oryzae reconstructs multiforisin H biosynthesis.
Two HR-PKSs supply distinct building blocks that are joined and tailored through the mfn pathway.
Transcriptomic co-regulation supports the proposed mfn locus boundaries in the native producer.
Current MIBiG retirement prevents treating BGC0003118 as an active validated physical record despite strong functional pathway evidence.
VrcA is a bifunctional sesterterpene synthase that converts IPP/DMAPP through GFPP to variecoladiene.
Coexpression of vrcA and vrcB yields variecolin and variecolactone, establishing VrcB as the oxidative tailoring enzyme.
Homologous P450 substitution expands the variecolin scaffold space and can alter activity/toxicity profiles.
J. minutella stromata contain structurally characterized minutellins A-D and hinnulin A.
Comparative Hypoxylaceae genomics supports an azaphilone BGC association, but exact minutellin gene-product causality remains correlative.
Current MIBiG retirement means BGC0003120 cannot be treated as an active validated physical record.
Deletion of the kotanin PKS gene abolishes the coumarin pathway and establishes the cluster's biosynthetic entry step.
KtnB and KtnC are required tailoring enzymes, with KtnC catalyzing regio- and stereoselective oxidative phenol coupling.
Native Ao415/Ao414 loss-of-function and metabolomics link the locus to desferriferrichrome biosynthesis.
Perturbing desferriferrichrome/iron homeostasis alters nematode-trap formation and predatory physiology.
Exogenous desferriferrichrome attenuates trap formation while increasing nematicidal activity in the reported system.
PeTS1 is a (+)-aristolochene synthase identified by heterologous screening of P. expansum terpene synthases.
MEP-pathway engineering and MBP fusion increased heterologous (+)-aristolochene production to 50 mg/L at 72 h.
The defining study does not establish the native activation state or downstream fungal tailoring pathway for PeTS1.
The dpfg/C16 programme can be reconstructed heterologously to generate FDDP-family products.
Native PH-1 PKS15 disruption abolishes FDDP-D and FDDP-E production in Q6 culture and infected wheat.
Native PH-1 terpene-synthase disruption strongly reduces FDDP-D/E, independently confirming the diterpene branch is required.
FDDP-D and FDDP-E are produced in planta during wheat-head infection.
Reduced disease phenotype after terpene-synthase disruption supports a virulence-associated role, but does not by itself establish the molecular host target of FDDP-D/E.
The 2020 reconstruction used F. graminearum 50218 as gene donor rather than PH-1; PH-1-specific native causality comes from the later CRISPR study.
Current MIBiG retirement prevents treating the historical physical record as an active validated database locus despite strong functional pathway evidence.
Physodic acid defines one P. furfuracea chemotype.
PF33-1_006185 / cluster 4 is the strongest published candidate for olivetoric/physodic acid biosynthesis.
Candidate cluster 4 contains a two-ACP NR-PKS, cytochrome P450 and monooxygenase among 10 genes.
The candidate cluster is nearly structurally identical in both chemotypes.
Regulation and/or epigenetic differences may determine depside versus depsidone chemotype.
Cytochrome P450 activity is a plausible determinant of ether-bond formation leading to physodic acid.
The retired MIBiG XXX physical placement cannot be repaired from candidate-cluster evidence alone.
mpsADFG expression generates macrophasetins A-C.
MpsD directs trans-decalin cyclization.
MpsF hydroxylates macrophasetin A toward macrophasetin C.
Native expression/ecological function in M. phaseolina remains unresolved.
A group-D TAS1 homologue biosynthesizes taslactam C-family γ-lactams.
The TAS1 homologue alone is sufficient for core fungal γ-lactam biosynthesis.
Taslactam C has proteasome inhibitory activity.
mlfA is required for Malformin A2/C biosynthesis in A. brasiliensis.
Complementation of ΔmlfA restores malformin production.
The F. oxysporum group-D TAS1 homologue biosynthesizes taslactam D-family γ-lactam chemistry.
The TAS1 homologue alone is sufficient for core fungal γ-lactam biosynthesis.
Proteasome inhibitory potency reported for taslactam C is not assigned to taslactam D without congener-specific evidence.
A. fabae pksAC is required for ascochitine biosynthesis.
AV22 contains a conserved homologous minimal 11-gene ascochitine cluster.
Ascochitine is not essential for tested A. fabae pathogenicity.
The A. fabae knockout is not an AV22 knockout.
The anu cluster is silent under tested native conditions but productive heterologously.
AnuG catalyzes final oxidative lactonization to (2S,9S)-annullatin D.
FUP1 is required for fusaproliferin biosynthesis.
FUP4 is required for oxidation toward terpestacin.
FUP5 acetylates terpestacin to fusaproliferin.
FUP2 remains less directly validated because a knockout was not obtained.
CpaA/CpaS synthesizes cAATrp.
CpaD prenylates cAATrp to β-CPA.
CpaO converts β-CPA to α-CPA and is required for native CPA production.
TvTS produces talaropentaene from DMAPP/IPP through HexPP.
TvTS is transcriptionally silent in native wild type under tested conditions.
amyB-promoter replacement activates TvTS and talaropentaene production in native T. verruculosus.
MpMS produces macrophomene through a non-squalene HexPP route.
MpMS PT and TC activities are resolved by active-site variants and structural enzymology.
The key study does not establish a native promoter-activation or transcriptional-silence phenotype for MpMS.
CgCS from C. gloeosporioides ES026 is sufficient to produce colleterpenol in heterologous yeast.
CgCS is a bifunctional prenyltransferase–terpene cyclase supporting a non-squalene triterpene route through HexPP.
The canonical WVTB01000012.1 interval is not asserted to be the exact experimentally tested ES026 locus without sequence reconciliation.
Native regulation and ecological role of colleterpenol biosynthesis remain unresolved.
P. ipomoeae IasaF13 produces a broad ergot-alkaloid profile in host-associated material.
The P. ipomoeae EAS locus contains functional orthologs spanning early clavine, lysergic-acid and late peptide/amidation stages.
Individual P. ipomoeae gene functions are not treated as direct genetic causality where the study relies on orthology.
The canonical strain string lasaF13 conflicts typographically with primary-literature IasaF13.
Native lpsB disruption in E. festucae Fl1 abolishes ergovaline production in infected perennial ryegrass.
Complementation of the lpsB mutant restores ergovaline pathway competence.
The lpsB mutant accumulates lysergic acid and fails to form the downstream lysergyl-alanine step, positioning LpsB in late ergovaline biosynthesis.
EAS pathway expression/product formation is strongly host-state dependent, with in-planta activity exceeding axenic culture.
The canonical source-category SQ_A label is a database metadata property and does not negate direct native lpsB causality.
P. ipomoeae IasaF13 is associated with a native host-derived profile containing paspaline, paxilline and multiple terpendoles.
The conserved idtG/idtM/idtB/idtC core supports assignment of the paspaline-producing indole-diterpene scaffold pathway.
Peripheral idtP/idtQ/idtK/idtF genes are associated with downstream indole-diterpene diversification, including terpendole congeners.
idtS remains functionally unresolved and no P. ipomoeae strain-specific knockout evidence is promoted for the listed IDT genes.
